stem.text: Ammonia exists as simple covalent molecules, $\text{NH}_3$. Ammonia can react with suitable reagents to form products containing ammonium ions, $\text{NH}_4^{+}$. Ammonia can also react with suitable reagents to form products containing amide ions, $\text{NH}_2^{-}$.
Which of these nitrogen-containing species are present in an aqueous solution of ammonia?
